title: Nagata lifting for complete Noetherian pairs
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. If $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] and $A/I$ is Nagata [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], then $A$ is Nagata.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1 Step 1 (1-3), printed p.8, and Appendix A, printed p.15: Marot’s lifting property for Nagata rings (reference [8]).

proof.text: It suffices to show every prime quotient $A/\mathfrak p$ is N-2. If any is not, choose such a prime $\mathfrak p$ maximal under inclusion. This choice follows from Noetherianity: an ascending chain of ideals has union an ideal, its finitely many generators lie in one term, so the chain stabilizes; hence any nonempty collection of ideals has a maximal member. Put $B=A/\mathfrak p$. The ideals of $B$ correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $\mathfrak p$, so $B$ is a Noetherian domain. For every nonzero prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, its inverse image strictly contains $\mathfrak p$, and $B/\mathfrak q$ is N-2 by maximality. This argument is vacuous, with the desired result, if $A$ has no primes.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, p.107, Noetherian induction on prime ideals.

proof.text: Let $J=IB=(I+\mathfrak p)/\mathfrak p$. The $A$-module $B$ is generated by $1$, so finite-module completeness makes $B$ complete and separated for $J$: the module powers $I^nB$ equal $J^n$. The natural quotient identifies $B/J$ with $A/(I+\mathfrak p)$, a quotient of $A/I$; Nagata quotient permanence therefore makes $B/J$ Nagata. The ideal $J$ is proper: otherwise $J^n=B$ for all $n$, contradicting separatedness of the nonzero domain $B$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, p.107, passage to B and its closed fibre; Stacks Tags 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor) and 032T (lemma-quasi-finite-over-nagata) supply the cited permanence facts.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary finite field extension $L/\operatorname{Frac}B$ and let $T$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $L$. Step 1 supplies exactly the Japanese proper prime quotients required by the normalization Noetherianity criterion; hence $T$ is Noetherian. Apply the adic normalization finiteness criterion to $(B,J,L,T)$: $B$ is a Noetherian domain, is $J$-complete, $J$ is proper, $B/J$ is Nagata, and $T$ is Noetherian. It follows that $T$ is finite over $B$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, p.107, using Lemma 1.2 and Proposition 2.1.

proof.text: Since $L$ was arbitrary, step 3 says precisely that $B$ is N-2. This contradicts the choice of $\mathfrak p$. Thus every prime quotient of $A$ is N-2; together with the given Noetherianity this is the definition of $A$ being Nagata.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q153-06f6bba55 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, both new nodes and every cited statement. Steps: (1) a maximal bad prime p exists by ACC, B=A/p is a Noetherian domain, and B/q is N-2 for every nonzero q; elementary and correct. (2) B is complete for J=IB by finite-module-complete (I^nB=J^n); B/J=A/(I+p) is Nagata by the 'in particular' clause of finite-over-nagata-nagata; J is proper by separatedness. (3) Step 1 supplies the hypotheses of japanese-quotients-noetherian-normalization, so T is Noetherian; Steps 1-2 and that result supply every hypothesis of adic-noetherian-normalization-finite, so T is finite. (4) The definitions close the contradiction. New nodes: both are statement-only, self-contained, true and strictly smaller than the item, not restated clauses. Small cases checked: field, DVR, J=0, redundant properness of J. Each was checked through the Krull/Mori-Nishimura route and through the minimal primes of JT plus Krull separation plus lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring.
